data.title: Stavudine & didanosine (older NRTIs)
data.summary: Antivirals & ART · Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors — stavudine (d4T, thymidine analogue) and didanosine (ddI, adenosine analogue)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors — stavudine (d4T, thymidine analogue) and didanosine (ddI, adenosine analogue)

## Mechanism of action
- Phosphorylated to triphosphates that terminate HIV DNA chains (mitochondrial DNA polymerase-γ inhibition explains toxicity)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Historical: stavudine-based first-line regimens (D4T/3TC/NVP, D4T/3TC/EFV) were widely used in India; phased out by WHO/NACO because of toxicity
- Important for exams because of their adverse effects

## Dose & formulations
- Stavudine 30 mg twice daily (historic); didanosine 400 mg once daily on an empty stomach (historic)

## Adverse effects
- Stavudine: lipoatrophy (facial and limb fat loss — the classic cause), painful peripheral neuropathy, lactic acidosis with hepatic steatosis, pancreatitis
- Didanosine: pancreatitis (can be fatal), peripheral neuropathy, lactic acidosis, non-cirrhotic portal hypertension
- Stavudine + didanosine together: fatal lactic acidosis in pregnancy — never combined

## Contraindications
- Never combine stavudine with zidovudine (antagonism) or with didanosine (toxicity)

## Drug interactions
- Hydroxyurea, ribavirin increase didanosine toxicity; tenofovir raises didanosine levels

## Pregnancy & lactation
Not used now.

## Viva points
- Stavudine → lipoatrophy (facial wasting) and neuropathy — reason for its withdrawal
- Mitochondrial toxicity of 'd-drugs' (d4T, ddI, ddC)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.4 (Stavudine, Didanosine; D4T/3TC/NVP regimens); Wolverton 4e ch.11. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
